History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
Adult female presents with an acute left-sided throbbing headache with visual aura, nausea, vomiting, and photophobia—clinical picture most consistent with migraine; counselled on symptomatic management, headache diary, and red-flag return precautions.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Severe throbbing headache on left side since mid-day today (onset a few hours ago).  
• Temporal profile: Aura of “zig-zag” lines and bilateral blurred vision a few minutes before pain onset; similar episode a few weeks ago that lasted ≈2 days.  
• Aggravating factors: Worsens with head/neck movement and leaning forward; bright light aggravates.  
• Relieving factors: None tried yet today; previously rested and used unspecified painkillers.  
• Associated symptoms: Nausea, two episodes of vomiting, photophobia.  
• ROS / pertinent negatives: No fever, rash, speech difficulty, limb weakness, balance problems, or recent head injury. No breathlessness.  
• Psychosocial concern: Significant anxiety about brain tumour due to friend’s family history.

Past Medical History:
• Denies chronic medical conditions.  
• No prior migraine diagnosis.

Medications:
• Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive) – dose/route/frequency not documented (on for 3 months).  
• Past episodic use of over-the-counter painkillers (names/doses not documented).

Allergies:
• Not documented.

Social History:
• Occupation: Fashion industry; reports high job stress.  
• Lives alone.  
• No tobacco use.  
• No alcohol use.  
• No recreational drug use reported.  
• Minimal exercise; no specific stress-relief activities.

Family History:
• Mother: Migraines; underactive thyroid.  
• No known family history of brain cancer or other neurologic disorders.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: not recorded.  
• General / neurological / other systems: not documented (patient not examined during recorded portion).

Investigations:
• None performed or available at this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Probable migraine with aura  
  • Plan:  
    – Symptomatic treatment: Paracetamol or Co-codamol, and an NSAID such as Ibuprofen or Naproxen (doses/route/frequency to be provided).  
    – Headache diary to identify frequency and triggers.  
    – Consider prophylactic migraine medication if attacks become more frequent or persistent; to be discussed at follow-up.  
    – Lifestyle advice: manage stress, regular meals, hydration, sleep hygiene, consider exercise.  
    – Safety-net: Return urgently if headache worsens or fails to respond to medication, or if develops neurological deficits (weakness, speech or vision changes), increasing neck pain, or other concerning symptoms.

General follow-up:  
  • Review in 1 week (earlier if red-flag symptoms) to reassess headache pattern and need for preventive therapy.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: Allergies, complete medication reconciliation, vital signs, physical examination findings.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; occasional conversational overlap but clinically adequate.
